newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-BAKER-FINCH DISQUALIFIED FROM NEW SOUTH WALES CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BAKER-FINCH DISQUALIFIED FROM NEW SOUTH WALES CHALLENGE.

text.p: Former British Open champion Ian Baker-Finch was disqualified from the New South Wales Challenge golf tournament on Friday for signing an incorrect score card.
The lead was shared five ways after the second round with Australians Peter Lonard, David Ecob, Chris Gray and Robert Stephens and New Zealand's Steve Alker all on seven-under-par 137.
Baker-Finch's miserable run of recent form hit a new low when he disqualified himself after realising he had signed an incorrect card after Thursday's opening round.
The Australian, who has made only one halfway cut in a tournament in more than two years, inadvertently signed for a first round of 78 when he had actually scored 79.
"I was careless leaving the scorers' hut because I was a bit disappointed at shooting seven over par and didn't check my card carefully enough," Baker-Finch told a news conference.
Australia's Peter Fowler was also disqualified after missing his tee-off time while compatriot Martyn Roberts withdrew before his second round through injury.
Roberts was struck on the wrist by a ball driven by an amateur playing partner during Wednesday's pro-am event.

Ecob began the day four shots behind overnight leader Gray but reached six under par after picking up four shots in three holes on his outward nine. He went on to card a five-under 67 while Gray shot a steady 71.
Australian Masters champion Lonard hit a 69 and Stephens a 68 while Alker, twice a winner on the Australasian PGA Tour this season, had a 70.
The leaders were one stroke clear of defending champion Peter Senior and fellow Australian Lucas Parsons.
Senior, who needs to win the tournament to guarantee a place in the British Open at Royal Troon in July, shot a 70.
